results.title: COVID-19 pandemic conditions affecting QoL and mental health of oncology patients in Poland

abstracts.content: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic has caused widespread disruptions in oncology care, significantly affecting both the quality of life (QoL) and mental health of cancer patients. This study aimed to evaluate the long-term impacts of the pandemic on oncology patients, focusing on the periods before, during, and after the pandemic. Objective: The objective of this study was to assess the changes in QoL, illness acceptance, and mental health indicators, including the risk of depression, generalized anxiety, elevated stress levels, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) among oncology patients, comparing these factors across the pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods. Material and Methods: This study included 2000 oncology patients, divided into three cohorts based on the time of assessment: pre-pandemic (2019, n = 600), during the pandemic (2020–2021, n = 800), and post-pandemic (2023, n = 600). This study included a balanced sample of 52% female and 48% male participants, with a mean age of 58 years (SD = 11.9), representing a wide range of cancer types including breast (25.7%), lung (20.9%), and colorectal cancer (14.8%). Additional demographics showed a mean BMI of 25.8, with varied educational levels, marital statuses, income levels, and lifestyle factors such as smoking and alcohol consumption. QoL was assessed using the EORTC QLQ-C30, while the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) was used to measure depression and anxiety. The PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) was used to evaluate PTSD symptoms, and stress levels were measured with the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS). Statistical analyses were conducted using ANOVA and chi-square tests to assess differences between the groups. Results: During the pandemic, the prevalence of depression symptoms rose significantly, from 15% pre-pandemic to 32% (p < 0.001), while the risk of generalized anxiety increased from 18% to 40% (p < 0.001). Stress levels also saw a sharp rise, with 45% of patients reporting elevated stress during the pandemic compared to 22% before (p < 0.001). The rate of PTSD symptoms increased from 10% pre-pandemic to 28% during the pandemic (p < 0.001). QoL scores dropped markedly, with the mean EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status score decreasing by 25% during the pandemic (p < 0.01). Illness acceptance declined, with 60% of patients reporting poor acceptance during the pandemic, compared to 35% before. In the post-pandemic period, a slight improvement was observed across all measures. Depression levels dropped to 28% (p < 0.05 compared to the pandemic period), and anxiety levels decreased to 35% (p < 0.05). Stress and PTSD symptoms also showed modest reductions, with 38% reporting elevated stress and 22% exhibiting PTSD symptoms (p < 0.05). However, these post-pandemic values remained significantly higher than pre-pandemic levels (p < 0.001). QoL improved marginally, with a 10% increase in the global health status score compared to the pandemic period, though it remained lower than pre-pandemic scores (p < 0.05). Conclusions: The COVID-19 pandemic had a profound impact on the mental health and QoL of oncology patients, with significant increases in depression, anxiety, stress, and PTSD symptoms, along with a decrease in QoL and illness acceptance. While post-pandemic recovery trends are apparent, the psychological burden remains elevated compared to pre-pandemic conditions. These findings highlight the need for continued mental health support and interventions for oncology patients, even after the immediate pandemic effects have subsided.

results.title: Ilustracjonizm i symbolizm w muzyce fortepianowej Sergiusza Rachmaninowa w kontekście tworzenia własnej koncepcji interpretacyjnej. Analiza zagadnienia na przykładzie wybranych Études-Tableaux

abstracts.content: Both cycles of Études-Tableaux (opuses 33 and 39, composed between 1911 and 1917 in Russia), piano poems combining virtuosity and elements of sound painting represent the mature period in the works by Sergei Rachmaninoff (1873–1943) – a pianist, composer and conductor – regarded as one of the most prominent figures of the Golden Age of the Piano, follower of Chopinian and Lisztian tradition which he extended by enhancing expressiveness, which resulted in the creation of an interesting piano texture. As an invaluable contribution to the solo piano literature, Études-Tableaux demonstrate the full tonal capabilities of the instrument, and their illustrative idiom coexisting with the symbolistic element opens up endless possibilities of artistic creation. Their distinguishing feature is the extramusical dimension along with obvious influences of Orthodox Church music and Russian folk music, a multitude of fascinating borrowings from the field of painting and musical metaphors. An integral component of developing one’s own interpretative concept involves an analysis of the narrative of Études-Tableaux in terms of symbolism as an ideological link to the full expression that affects their unique poetics. A few Études have been explored in order to identify the sources of inspirations, extramusical analogies, comparative elements and stylistic reminiscences that refer to the creativity of composers highly regarded by Rachmaninoff. The conveyance of hidden meanings shall be done through the composer’s complex musical rhetoric introducing the artistic anxiety that inspires a constant search for musical meanings. The process of interpretation becomes a meta-journey leading deeper into the fascinating world of Rachmaninovian symbolism, extending the scope of imagination with parallels from the borderland between literature and painting of Russian (Lermontov, Vrubel, Levitan, Kustodiev) and European (Perrault, Böcklin) art.

otherTitles.title: Illustrationism and Symbolism in Sergei Rachmaninoff’s Piano Music in the Context of Creating Own Interpretative Concept. An Analysis of the Issue in Selected Études-Tableaux

abstracts.content: The musical genres that the avant-garde of the 1960s and 1970s rejected as nothing more than a set of time-honoured rules, continue to inspire contemporary composers in their exploration of new forms of musical language. Such an affinity is present in numerous piano concertos written by Polish composers at the turn of the 21st century. The article presents the results of research and analysis in relation to the composition King of the Cosmos Disappears. Concerto for Orchestra, Threads and Piano by Aleksander Nowak, an intriguing example of the piano concerto genre in the oeuvre of a representative of the ‘middle generation’ of contemporary Polish composers. A number of innovative ideas used in the composition concern both the treatment of the core principles of the genre and the approach to the piano part.

journal.title: Gdansk Journal of East Asian Studies

abstracts.content:
Wietnam – państwo w Azji Południowo-Wschodniej ze względu na bardzo dogodny klimat, wielokilometrowe piaszczyste plaże z ciepłą wodą w Morzu Wschodnim, a także wyjątkowe zasoby antropogeniczne stanowi jeden z większych potencjałów turystycznych Azji. Dodatkowym argumentem jest także wysoka pozycja w kolejnym indeksie światowego bezpieczeństwa, w którym Wietnam zajmując miejsce 41, zanotował wzrost o 4 pozycje rok do roku. Najczęściej odwiedzane przez turystów: Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City, Hoi An, Da Nang, Nha Trang, Zatoka Ha Long, największa jaskinia świata Son Dong, wieże byłego królestwa Champa, górskie atrakcje w Ha Giang, rejsy w Tam Coc, tarasowe pola ryżowe Moc Chau, rajskie wyspy – to jedynie ułamek zasobów turystycznych Wietnamu. Dwa tygodnie, które przeciętny turysta poświęca na zwiedzanie, nie pozwalają na odkrycie wielu skarbów kultury w północnej, środkowej i południowej
części kraju. Skarby narodowe Wietnamu i inne cenne artefakty znajdują się przede wszystkim w muzeach, ale także w świątyniach (głównie pagodach), świątyniach literatury, cytadelach oraz w kompleksach świątynnych, przede wszystkim w północnej części kraj Kompleks świątynny Pho Hien stanowi zwartą przestrzeń organizacyjną, powiązaną XVI–XVII-wieczną historią, religią buddyjską, położeniem w stolicy prowincji Hung Yen, atrakcyjnością turystyczną, powszechną dostępnością, a także spójnymi narzędziami marketingowymi w postaci: materiałów promocyjnych, publikacji naukowych i koncepcji zagospodarowania Pho Hien. Wśród możliwości rozwojowych kompleksu należy wymienić przede wszystkim: podejmowane wspólne próby spójnego zagospodarowania turystycznego, festiwal kompleksu Pho Hien, spójną promocję turystyczną, na billboardach i w biurach turystycznych. W przekonaniu autora przedstawionym w pracy zagrożeniom (marginalizacja kompleksu, brak środków fi nansowych, niedostateczna promocja, niewdrażanie koncepcji zagospodarowania, powielanie przestarzałych rozwiązań organizacyjnych, niezrównoważony rozwój gospodarczy) należy przeciwstawić zaproponowane powyżej rozwiązania organizacyjne i marketingowe, co umożliwi stworzenie z tego miejsca jedną z najbardziej popularnych atrakcji turystycznych w Wietnamie.

results.title: The Beggar’s Opera Johna Gaya – między sztuką wyższą a kulturą popularną

abstracts.content: This article is an attempt to present the history of the creation of John Gay’s work The Beggar’s Opera and the extremely important role that it has played in shaping the popular English-language music theatre. This piece is sometimes even considered a distant ancestor of the modern musical. The text outlines the historical, economic and cultural background of the creation of the work (relating, among others, to significant milestones in the development of opera, especially in the British Isles) and analyses its characteristic features, which made not only the original production of 1728 extremely popular, but also created an interest in this timeless classic in general, especially in the Anglo-Saxon cultural milieu. The article discusses the issues relating to the parody of the then-opera theatre and a critique of the social and political situation in Great Britain at the beginning of the 18th century in The Beggar’s Opera. Gay’s piece is shown as appealing to the popular tastes of London theatre audiences, but at the same time as an innovative work that introduces previously unknown elements to the stage of musical theatre, using on a large scale the techniques that later became characteristic of burlesque (travesty, pastiche) and in fact starting a new genre, ballad opera.

otherTitles.title: The Beggar’s Opera by John Gay: Between High Art and Popular Culture

results.title: Od młodzieńczego rozmachu ku neoklasycznej elegancji. Fortepianowe juwenilia Zygmunta Mycielskiego ze zbioru Szkice kompozycyjne 1927

abstracts.content: The Zygmunt Mycielski Archive is housed in the National Library of Poland in Warsaw. One of the volumes in this collection is a draft signed by the composer, entitled Sketches of Composition 1927. It contains early musical pieces by Zygmunt Mycielski: songs, pieces for piano and chamber music. They were written between 1927 and 1938, first in Wiśniowa and Kraków, then in Paris during Mycielski’s studies with Paul Dukas and Nadia Boulanger, and after returning to Poland, in Vilnius and Bukowina Tatrzańska. Interpreted with the help of letters to mother Maria Mycielska née Szembek, they allow us to reconstruct the creative process, informal instructions from Karol Szymanowski, and learn about the young artist’s preferences.

results.title: Protective structures as a device of ensuring the safety of victims in a war situation

abstracts.content: Interest  in  protective  structures  is  steadily  increasing  as  the  armed  conflict  in  Ukraine  unfolds. Experience shows that shelters and hiding places are the most effective form of protection for civilians from conventional and unconventional war threats. Meanwhile, there are no guidelines and rules for the construction of public and private shelters in Poland. The problem is a big one, especially in view of the war that is taking place in the close vicinity of Poland. The purpose of the article is to review Polish and foreign  legal  and  organizational  solutions  in  the  field  of  protective  constructions  and  to  indicate  the technical requirements necessary to meet in a situation of war danger, with particular emphasis on the use of nuclear weapons. The authors put forward the thesis that in the face of military and non-military threats,  the  effective  way  to  protect  and  defend  the  life  and  health  of  the  population  are  properly maintained  and  managed  protective  structures,  including  shelters  and  hiding  places  and  places  of temporary shelter. However, the basic problem remains the question of legal regulation in this regard and  the  responsibility  for  their  financing  and  maintenance,  which  involves  the  issueof  ownership (private and public shelters). In Poland, the experience of other countries that have adopted a variety of solutions should be a guideline for forward-looking activities in the area of protective structures.

results.title: From Vlasov Equation to Degenerate Nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard Equation

abstracts.content: We provide a rigorous mathematical framework to establish the hydrodynamic limit of the Vlasov model introduced in Takata and Noguchi (J. Stat. Phys. 172:880-903, 2018) by Noguchi and Takata in order to describe phase transition of fluids by kinetic equations. We prove that, when the scale parameter tends to 0, this model converges to a nonlocal Cahn-Hilliard equation with degenerate mobility. For our analysis, we introduce apropriate forms of the short and long range potentials which allow us to derive Helmhotlz free energy estimates. Several compactness properties follow from the energy, the energy dissipation and kinetic averaging lemmas. In particular we prove a new weak compactness bound on the flux.

results.title: High-Performance Structures of Biopolymer Gels Activated with Scleroprotein Crosslinkers

abstracts.content: The study explores innovative crosslinking processes for biopolymer gel materials using amino acids and ion-redox initiators to significantly enhance their structural and functional properties. Advanced analytical techniques, including FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, XRD, TEM, TGA, DSC, ToF-SIMS, SEM/EDS, GPC/SEC, and elemental analysis, were employed for comprehensive material characterization. The synthesized materials show potential applications in packaging and medicine, particularly for single-use products with short life cycles. Two crosslinking strategies were developed. The first combines gelatin with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA); keratin hydrolysate; and amino acids such as cysteine, hydroxyproline, proline, and histidine. The second employs endogenous cysteine, activated by ion-redox initiators, leveraging its trans-sulfuration ability to form highly stable polymer networks with optimized mechanical and thermal properties. Notably, the synergy between cysteine and potassium persulfate redox initiators proved particularly effective, making this approach attractive for industrial applications. This study introduces novel crosslinking methods and highlights the potential of amino acid-based strategies for designing advanced biopolymer gels with enhanced properties.

results.title: Pathological buying on the rise? Compensative and compulsive buying in Poland in the pre- and (Post-)pandemic times

abstracts.content: The study concerns the development of compensative and compulsive buying in Poland comparing the results of three waves of a cross-sectional study conducted before and at the end of the COVID-19 pandemic. Six predictors of susceptibility to compensative and compulsive buying are in focus: materialism, self-esteem, gender, age, frequency of online shopping, and experience of the COVID-19 pandemic. However, the importance of the first four predictors in explaining compensative and compulsive buying is already very well described in the literature, while the novelty consists in the predictive model including the variables that describe frequency of online shopping and negative experiences related to the COVID-19 pandemic, such as coronavirus infection, hospitalization or death of a loved one. On the one hand, a stronger susceptibility to compensative and compulsive buying could be a reaction to these negative experiences of the pandemic; on the other hand, the increased frequency of online shopping as a result of the pandemic may be an important factor in the development of compensative and compulsive buying due to the easy implementation of purchase acts and weaker social control. To achieve the above research objectives, the German Compulsive Buying Indicator (GCBI) was used to measure susceptibility to compensative and compulsive buying. The data were obtained within three waves of the study (2010, 2019, 2022) based on a random sample of about 1,000 respondents representing statistically the general adult population. Drawing on this study, the prevalence of compensative and compulsive buying is observed at 12–19% and 2–4%. The predictors of GCBI are materialism, self-esteem, gender in all examined models and additionally age, frequency of online shopping, and experience of the COVID-19 pandemic in selected models. Although the findings related to the role of materialism, self-esteem, and gender in the prediction of GCBI reflect the results reported in the literature, the analogous conclusions about age, online shopping, and experiences with the COVID-19 pandemic are different from the established opinions. The commonly reported effect of age becomes statistically significant when the examined population is limited to Gens Y and Z. Although extensive online shopping co-exists with compensative and compulsive buying in the total population, the obtained data lead to reverse conclusions in the case of women’s subpopulation representing Gens Y and Z. The negative experience with the COVID-19 pandemic operationalised as hospitalization of a close friend predicts GCBI, but again only in the case of representatives of Gens Y and Z, especially among women. The findings show how important the creation of appropriate intervention strategies is within the consumer policy directed to representatives of the younger generations who may develop pathological buying as a response to negative experiences such as COVID-19 pandemic. The findings can inform of the goals behind therapeutic support for compulsive buyers, and implications for social work. People affected by excessive compensative or compulsive buying need to be given opportunities to build up their strengths and growth of their psychological resources towards healthy self-esteem, which seems to be the best protection against excessive compensative and compulsive buying.

The use and application of artificial intelligence (AI) in decision-making processes

journal.title: Silesian University of Technology Scientific Papers. Organization & Management

abstracts.content: Purpose: The aim of the study was to analyze and characterize the available tools in decision making processes using artificial intelligence. Design/methodology/approach: The article uses the method of text analysis together with the technique of content analysis. It was also supported by empirical research on the use of AI tools in decision-making processes. The article focuses on the areas of application of AI in decision making processes; AI tools used decision-making processes and use in business are characterized. The benefits and disadvantages of these tools and the ethical implications of using AI by managers are indicated. Findings: Although the use of AI tools cannot work on their own, initiate thought processes or define threats and benefits, trends in this field are evolving along with technological progress. AI already plays a key role in decision-making processes and its scope will increase. Research limitations/implications: The development of AI should be constantly monitored. The identified threat is the use of NLP techniques in the tools used, which can lead to manipulation both by decision-makers and by decision-makers. Practical implications: Growing trust in AI tools in business gives opportunities for faster decision-making without human error. It is advisable to use them in practice to reduce the time of decision-making and reduce the risk of human error in this process. Social implications: AI is the future happening today. It is impossible to avoid the use of artificial intelligence by humans. The benefits of AI are greater than the risks at this point. As a result, many industries need to use AI tools in their practice to stay on the market, and customers and contractors put pressure on such activities by trusting these tools. Originality/value: The article is dedicated to managers who want to use AI in their professional practice, who are not yet convinced.

results.title: Artysta i filozof. Roman Maciejewski jako twórca duetów fortepianowych

abstracts.content: Roman Maciejewski has a unique and charismatic personality. His fulfilling life and varied artistic career may intrigue and provoke us to look into his work. The composer of the great Requiem does not enjoy popularity and although his name is known in the musical circles, his works are rarely performed. Undoubtedly, this is a loss for Polish music repertoire, and its impoverishment. In this lecture devoted to Maciejewski, I would like to introduce the figure of this composer as a man and artist, but also as a philosopher. His life was full of ideas that had a significant impact on his music and professional decisions. My main interests are compositions for piano duo, which seems particularly interesting in the context of the relatively limited Polish repertoire for this type of chamber ensemble. Pieces for piano duo falls into three categories: originals, arrangements and transcriptions. Maciejewski’s original works include Piano Duo Concertante (1936), Allegro Concertante (1936), Kołysanka i Tarantela (1938), Oberek (1943) and Mazurek (1951). Arranged music, i.e. pieces based on a popular melody but enriched with the composer’s creativity, thanks to which they essentially become original compositions: Tańce szwedzkie (1940–42) and Negro Spirituals (1943). Transposed music comprises 23 compositions representing various styles and genres. This paper was prepared on the basis of Roman Maciejewski’s own experience in performing piano duos.

otherTitles.title: Artist and philosopher Roman Maciejewski as a composer of piano duets

results.title: Quatre Mendiants et Quatre Hors d’Oeuvres – w muzycznym salonie Gioachino Rossiniego

abstracts.content: From among the 109 works by Rossini originally written for piano, the vast majority (101) were written at the end of the composer’s life between 1857 and 1868. 95 of them, along with other instrumental and vocal compositions, he collected and arranged in thirteen volumes under one title, Sins of Old Age. Rossini’s typical sense of humour coupled with his distance from creativity and himself is visible in many of them. However, it manifests itself in a special way in the fourth volume of the collection, Quatre Mendiants et Quatre Hors d’Oeuvres. In France, the term ‘mendiants’ defined four types of dried fruit and nuts: figs, almonds, raisins and hazelnuts; such are also the titles of the subsequent works by Rossini. For the set of four Hors d’Oeuvres, or snacks, Rossini chose ‘Les radis’ (radishes), ‘Les anchovies’ (anchovy preserves), ‘Les cornichons’ (gherkins) and ‘La beurre’ (butter). This seemingly ‘gastronomic’ album, especially its first part, is in fact a very personal, musical depiction of everyday home life presented with a playful wink. Learning these works better, it is easy to understand why the acknowledged master, who had been silent in the field of opera for years, would not agree to publish his latest works. In the outside musical world of the time, in the moment of triumph of the music by Wagner, Brahms and Schumann, his intimate, playful compositions were something unique. At the same time, however, the latter did not follow the dominant style. Enjoying great fame and fortune, Rossini could afford to put his compositions on the shelf, as it were, presenting his works only to a small group of friends and guests invited to the composer’s villa in Passy. The first complete edition of Quatre Mendiants et Quatre Hors d’Oeuvres was published thanks to Fondazione Rossini in Pesaro as late as in 1976.

otherTitles.title: Quatre Mendiants et Quatre Hors d’Oeuvres – in Gioachino Rossini’s Music Salon

results.title: Życie i działalność Edwina Kowalika (1928–1997)

abstracts.content: On 20 May 2022, 25 years have passed since the death of Edwin Kowalik. This anniversary is the perfect moment to remind the Polish music community of this great pianist, composer and community arts worker. Edwin Kowalik was born in 1928 in Chropaczów (today a district of Świętochłowice) who completely lost his eyesight in his childhood. However, at the music school in Laski (today named after the pianist), his extraordinary musical talents were discovered: eventually, Edwin Kowalik graduated from the Academy of Music in Łódź (he studied with Władysław Kędra and Maria Wiłkomirska). His performance was acclaimed in numerous competitions, including the 5th edition of Fryderyk Chopin International Piano Competition (honourable mention) and the International Piano Competition in Rio de Janeiro (1957, country representative, sixth prize). In addition to frequent concert performances in Poland and abroad, Kowalik worked as an editor and publisher of Braille notes in the Polish Association of the Blind, and together with the Fryderyk Chopin Society led to the publication of ‘Complete Works’ of Fryderyk Chopin and ‘Selected Works’ of Karol Szymanowski using the Braille system. Kowalik also found fulfilment in being the editor of Magazyn Muzyczny which he founded, writing poetry and composing, mainly short pieces for piano and simple song forms. So far, two documentaries, albeit not widely available, and one feature-reminiscence have appeared about the life and activities of Kowalik. This article is aimed at presenting the most important biographical information about Edwin Kowalik and his artistic ideas.

otherTitles.title: The Life and Work of Edwin Kowalik (1928–1997)

results.title: Zmierzch Bogów. Claude-Bénigne Balbastre – muzyka organowa czasów rewolucji

abstracts.content: Old French music used to be confined to the once coined term ‘golden age’ covering the years 1600–1789. However, during these nearly two hundred years French art underwent as significant stylistic changes as the rest of Europe. It is difficult to compare Titelouze’s early works with the music of composers of the late Enlightenment. The obvious connections between the emergence of these artists and a specific tradition are based on a common denominator which is the characteristic French organ of that time and on a specific, emblematic way of selecting voices and using colours. However, musical ideas underwent major transformations, and the political situation left its mark on the musical language of the composers of the second half of the 18th century. Social demand changed the recipient from the elitist to the egalitarian who interpreted all courtliness as a connection with the system against which successive states rebelled. Little is said about the situation of organ music during the revolution, except that the revival of this art was the establishment of a new school led by Cesar Franck and Jacques Nicolaus Lemmens. The situation of church music, including organ music, was extremely precarious because the church as an institution became one of the targets of the revolutionaries’ attacks. Ending with the outbreak of the French Revolution, the organ music of the second half of the 18th century is characterized by the simplification of means of expression, striving for the greatest possible clarity and readability.

otherTitles.title: Twilight of the Gods. Claude-Bénigne Balbastre – the Organ Music of the Revolutionary Times

results.title: Polifonia w białoruskiej muzyce fortepianowej na przełomie XX–XXI w.

abstracts.content: Belarusian music is an integral part of European musical culture. But many of its aspects still require more detailed consideration and coverage in musicological publications. The article is devoted to studying the polyphony in the Belarusian piano music at the turn of the 21st century. The purpose of the research was to show the specific aesthetic and technical qualities of polyphony in the creative activity of different generations of composers. The research subject was the music collection Полифонические произведения белорусских композиторов для фортепиано (‘Polyphonic Works for Piano by Belarusian Composers’) published in 2019. It contains opuses by composers who began to write in different decades of the 20th and 21st centuries. This article contains a brief historical overview of musical culture, providing the context of the emergence of polyphony in Belarusian piano music. The artistic content of the compositions correlated with the poetics of postmodernism in its various manifestations. Methods of musicological and comparative analysis were used in the course of the study. The research results reveal that the composers’ aesthetic foundations are different. Yet, in general, Belarusian composers interpret polyphonic techniques and forms within the framework of European musical art.

results.title: Metody tworzenia skal muzycznych w improwizacji na podstawie skali durowej i molowej

abstracts.content: In this article entitled ‘Methods of Building Musical Scales in Improvisation on the Basis of the Major and Minor Scale’ I have highlighted the problem of multiplicity of the different scales and their transpositions which an improviser is obliged to master. Having assumed that an educated musician is able to use all the transpositions of the major and minor scale, I have proposed several solutions for creating modal and certain non-modal scales. Therefore I have identified the way to build the modal scales starting with consecutive degrees of the major (or minor) scale and presented both the advantages and disadvantages of that method. As an alternative, or a supplement, I have devised a method based on the analysis of the role of particular degrees of the music scale that may be treated as a characteristic feature of that scale. Next, I have suggested a solution consisting of adding these features to the selected major or minor scale, resulting in a desired transposition of the modal, or any other, scale. In the text I have raised the issue of creating the harmonic context for particular scales.

results.title: André Le Nôtre i barokowe ogrody francuskie

abstracts.content: André Le Nôtre was one of the greatest French landscape architects. For finance minister Nicolas Fouquet he designed the château grounds of Vaux-le-Vicomte near Melun (1656–61), adjusting his layout to suit the relief of the ground. He extended from the parterres great blocks of trees contracting progressively to accentuate the perspective, and related them to the fountains, the waterworks and the statuary, obtaining maximum reflection by drawing attention to water levels. So delighted with the result was Louis XIV that he charged Le Nôtre with planning the gardens at Versailles, where the grounds covered more than 15,000 acres (6,000 hectares). Transforming a muddy swamp into a park of magnificent vistas, he extended and enhanced the architecture of the palace, and his monumental style reflected and heightened the splendour of Louis XIV’s court.

results.title: Specyfika prowadzenia głosu w pieśniach kabaretowych Arnolda Schönberga (Brettl–Lieder) i Benjamina Brittena (Cabaret Songs)

abstracts.content: The cabaret song form appeared at some point in the lives of the Austrian representative of dodecaphony in music, Arnold Schönberg (Sieben Brettl-Lieder), and the 39 years younger British composer, Benjamin Britten (Four Cabaret Songs), providing a very interesting compilation of cabaret lightness and classical technical perfection. This original music represents an interesting and fascinating trend in the oeuvre of these eminent composers inspiring ambitious singers around the world. Both cycles share good and original poetry. In Schönberg’s case, it is the lyric poetry of German poets writing with the developing literary cabaret in mind, while in Britten’s, the philosophical and existential poetry of Wystan Hugh Auden, his mentor and friend. The author analyses not only the musical and literary layer of the songs, but discusses in detail the right kind of interpretation, the specific aspect of voice leading, the style of performance and all the nuances of the artistic interpretation of these songs. She analyses Schönberg’s characteristic Sprechgesang style as well as Britten’s swinging style with virtuosic elements and a wide vocal range.

results.title: Voluntary Johna Stanleya – kompozycja czy improwizowana forma? Inne spojrzenie na organową twórczość kompozytora

abstracts.content: John Stanley (1712–1786) went down in history as the composer of voluntaries, i.e. pieces of organ music, popular at the time, played during religious services of the Anglican Church. Usually improvised, voluntaries were composed by organists as early as in the 16th century. Many of them were actually written down, and later also printed, which is how we discovered these pieces. This article presents a profile of the composer and his artistic career, with reference to his disability (Stanley lost his sight as a result of an accident at the age of two). His notable contribution to the development of the already established genre of voluntary may be found in his three collections of voluntaries published during his lifetime. The composer popularized the two-movement structure, and the style of his music demonstrates that he was familiar with the works of the great masters of the era, such as Handel or Corelli. With many of his works being officially published, Stanley paved the way for an increase in the umber of published organ works. The article draws attention to Stanley’s flair for improvisation, which was known and admired throughout London. The article also addresses the question of writing down music played during live performances; to what extent being aware of the origin of voluntaries, as well as knowledge of the composer’s talent for improvisation, may influence the contemporary performances of Stanley’s works.

otherTitles.title: John Stanley’s Voluntary: A Composition or an Improvised form? A Fresh Look at the Composer’s Organ Works

An introduction to Ventra: a programmable abdominal phantom for training, educational, research, and development purposes.

abstracts.content: Background: Intra-abdominal pressure (IAP) is a critical parameter in the care of critically ill patients, as elevated IAP can lead to reduced cardiac output and organ perfusion, potentially resulting in multiple organ dysfunction and failure. The current gold standard for measuring IAP is an indirect technique via the bladder. According to the Abdominal Compartment Society’s Guidelines, new measurement methods/devices for IAP must be validated against the gold standard. Objectives: This study introduces Ventra, an abdominal phantom designed to simulate different IAP levels, abdominal compliance, respiration-related IAP variations, and bladder dynamics. Ventra aims to facilitate the development and validation of new IAP measurement devices while reducing reliance on animal and cadaveric studies. Additionally, it offers potential applications in training and education for biomedical engineering students. This study provides a thorough explanation on the phantom’s design and fabrication, which provides a low-cost solution for advancing IAP measurement research and education. The design concept, technical aspects, and a series of validation experiments determining whether Ventra is a suitable tool for future research are presented in this study. Methods: Ventra’s performance was evaluated through a series of validation tests using a pressure gauge and two intra-gastric (Spiegelberg and CiMON) and two intra-bladder (Accuryn and TraumaGuard) pressure measurement devices. The mean and standard deviation of IAP recordings by each device were investigated. Bland–Altman analysis was used to evaluate bias, precision, limits of agreement, and percentage error for each system. Concordance analysis was performed to assess the ability of Ventra in tracking IAP changes. Results: The phantom demonstrated excellent agreement with reference pressure measurements, showing an average bias of 0.11 ± 0.49 mmHg. A concordance coefficient of 100% was observed for the phantom as well. Ventra accurately simulated different abdominal compliances, with higher IAP values resulting in lower compliance. Abdominal volume changes showed a bias of 0.08 ± 0.07 L/min, and bladder fill volume measurements showed an average difference of 0.90 ± 4.33 mL for volumes ranging from 50 to 500 mL. Conclusion: The validation results were in agreement with the research guidelines of the world abdominal society. Ventra is a reliable tool that will facilitate the development and validation of new IAP measurement devices. It is an effective educational tool for biomedical engineering students as well.

results.title: The Acute Effects of Combined Isometric and Plyometric Conditioning Activities on Sprint Acceleration and Jump Performance in Elite Junior Sprinters

abstracts.content: This study investigates the acute effects of a combined isometric and plyometric unilateral conditioning activity (CA) on post-activation performance enhancement (PAPE) in junior elite sprinters. The rationale for combining isometric and plyometric exercises lies in their complementary effects: isometric exercises enhance neuromuscular activation, while plyometric exercises may exploit the stretch–shortening cycle to maximize power output. Thirteen sprinters (10 males, three females) performed countermovement jumps (CMJ) and 50 m sprints before and after the CA protocol, which involved Bulgarian split squats (15% body mass) and single-leg hops. Performance metrics, including sprint times, CMJ height, and modified reactive strength index (RSImod), were recorded and analyzed. Results showed a significant improvement in CMJ height (2.6 ± 3.1%, p < 0.001) and RSI (4.1 ± 7.5%, p = 0.038), alongside a reduction in 20 m sprint time (−0.8 ± 1.4%, p = 0.012). No significant changes were observed in 40 m and 50 m sprint times or ground contact and flight times. These findings suggest that the applied CA selectively enhances sprint acceleration and vertical jumping performance, with a minimal impact on sprint distances above 20 m. This study underscores the potential of incorporating combined isometric and plyometric CAs into sprint training to optimize short-distance performance, though further research is needed to refine exercise protocols and explore long-term effects.

abstracts.content: This article focuses on the mid-18th-century French instrumental music. The text is based on the factual information about the life and work of Jean Baptiste Barrière, who was highly regarded in Paris at the time as a cello virtuoso and a composer. He created a unique collection of music, the sixth volume of Harpsichord Sonatas and other six pieces. It should be noted that this is the first collection of harpsichord sonatas written by the French composer. It is also interesting to note that five of the sonatas in the collection are the author’s transcriptions of sonatas for viol pardessus accompanied by basso continuo from his fifth volume. This great and unique music is still barely known and should be featured more often in today’s concert programmes. The wealth of musical ideas, imagination and novelty are the elements that give quality to this music. They also make it attractive to the contemporary performers and audiences.

otherTitles.title: Jean Baptiste Barrière and His Harpsichord Book VI

results.title: Typy arii w twórczość G.F. Haendla

abstracts.content: The aria genres that we may find in Handelian repertoire follow the Italian opera seria tradition. The structure of the late-Baroque aria, perpetuated by Mattheson, usually takes the form of an aria da capo also in Haendel's works; following the Italian model, we may distinguish in it such parts as exordium, narratio prepositio, confutatio, confirmatio and the crowning peroratio. The arias that we may find in Haendel’s works, despite their similar formal structure, are diverse in terms of the emotion, i.e. the affect that they express. We may distinguish such types of arias as the tender aria cantabile, the majestic aria di portamento, the aria di mezzocarattere full of doubt, the violent aria agitata, the virtuosic aria di bravura or the aria concertata inspired by a solo concerto, along with its three variants (aria simile, aria di guerra, aria di caccia). Each aria is accompanied by a wide range of expressive means to emphasize the main emotion. An important element, at the performer’s discretion, is the choice of ornamentation appropriate to the character of the aria and the manner of its performance.

otherTitles.title: Types of arias in the works of G.F. Haendel

results.title: Scherzo jako organowa forma improwizowana. Skrótowa analiza wybranych autorskich przykładów muzycznych w kontekście wykonawczym

abstracts.content: Organ improvisation remains linked to symphonic music, which has inspired performers to search for an attractive sound, and to shape works based on formal patterns established over the centuries. When improvising virtuoso organ forms, the individual characteristics of the organist-improviser, such as speed of decision-making, motor coordination and ergonomics in the playing technique, as well as musical imagination, play a key role. The shape of the improvised organ symphonic scherzo is influenced by factors related to a thorough knowledge of the musical elements and the ability to distinguish and define the elements of a given style or musical language. Also crucial here is the degree of technical preparation in keyboard and pedal playing. Advanced works from the piano repertoire remain the appropriate model and area of inspiration for organists to improvise virtuosic forms. An analysis of the recorded scherzos provided a glimpse into the formal course and a general definition of the means of performance. The author hopes that an analytical view of improvised organ pieces will enable young students of music, interested in practising this complex art of immediate music-making on the instrument, to go through the creative process and increase the artistic value of their works. This is particularly important in the context of a marked increase in interest in the art of improvisation that we are seeing today in church music circles and among young organ virtuosos.

otherTitles.title: Scherzo as an Improvised Organ Form. A Brief Analysis of Selected Original Musical Examples in a Performance Context
